newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle crew set up space laboratory.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle crew set up space laboratory.

text.p: The crew of the space shuttle Columbia set up its orbiting laboratory on Wednesday and began a 16-day research programme.
The shuttle's crew of seven, which blasted off Tuesday, was working in two shifts to operate a $86 million suite of scientific experiments around the clock.

It was a second chance for astronauts to accomplish their research. Their first attempt at the mission in April was cut short after only five days aloft because of a troublesome electricity generator aboard Columbia.
The astronauts are working on 33 major experiments, including one in which they will light more than 100 controlled fires to study the behaviour of flame in space.

The shuttle crew caught a brief glimpse of the Russian Mir space station Wednesday morning. The two craft were about 60 miles (96 km) apart and in entirely different orbits. A docking on this mission was not possible.
Columbia and its crew are not due back to earth until July 17.
